extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers seeking magazine publication (particularly science fiction writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice for writers submitting short fiction to magazines (with examples from Asimov's and other genre markets). Focuses on submission strategy, market reading, handling rejection, and persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the best story you can
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the best story you can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author emphasizes that the fundamental requirement is simply to write the best story you can and submit quality work to top markets. There is no secret beyond producing strong writing; he frames his own practice as writing his best and submitting to the best markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know — i.e., read — the market you submit to
rubrics_metrics.description: Know — ie, read — the market you submit to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a long-time reader/subscriber gives a sense of the types of stories a magazine is likely to accept. Read the magazine to understand its tastes and the kinds of fiction it publishes; this helps determine likely fits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit stories that match the market's focus / genre fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit stories appropriate to the magazine's focus (e.g., Asimov's focuses on science fiction stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author generally submits science fiction to Asimov's because of its editorial focus. Examples show genre-fit matters in choosing where to send a story even if acceptance is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't take rejection personally
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections are routine and not personal; editors may provide useful feedback (the author cites receiving constructive comments from Asimov's editor Sheila Williams). Expect and accept rejections as part of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a story is rejected, submit it somewhere else
rubrics_metrics.description: When a story is rejected make sure to submit it somewhere else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep sending rejected stories to other markets—many stories rejected by one magazine were later accepted elsewhere (examples: stories rejected by Asimov's later accepted by Interzone and Apex). Maintain momentum by resubmitting rather than shelving work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be persistent with both your writing and your submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be persistent with both your writing and your submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistence across years of writing and submissions is necessary; the author documents many submissions over time, including eventual acceptances after earlier rejections, demonstrating the value of long-term persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect unpredictability; there is no guaranteed 'secret sauce'
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond the listed practices there is no secret to publishing your short stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author's submission history shows an irregular pattern of acceptances and rejections even when submitting seemingly appropriate work. Accept that outcomes are often unpredictable and there may be no clear pattern to success.
